He pulls them away and says she can't have one because she didn't ask, just grabbed. Then others asked and he gave them some, but when M pleads and apologizes, he still refuses because he thinks she's only apologizing because he said no. Now, moral acceptability. Let's think about social norms. When someone takes food without asking, especially grabbing it, that's rude. It's reasonable to expect people to ask before taking something that's yours. So if M just lunged at it without saying anything, that's not polite. He has the right to control his own food. If he's the owner, he can decide who gets to eat it. So if someone takes without permission, it's okay to refuse.

But then when M apologized and asked nicely, he still refused. Is that okay?
